recorded.final_text:
Yes! *UVA Library provides free full online access to The New York Times* for the entire University community (faculty, staff, and students) — this includes current news plus the archive back to 1851, world news, politics, opinion, business, arts, book reviews, NYT Magazine, and even Spanish/Chinese editions.

*How to access it:*
1. Go to the login/proxy link: <https://proxy1.library.virginia.edu/login?url=https://ezmyaccount.nytimes.com/grouppass/redir|Create your free NYT account via UVA Library>
2. Sign up using your UVA (or school-specific, e.g. Darden) email address to activate a *Group Pass*.
3. If you're off-Grounds, turn on the *VPN* before creating your account (not needed for regular reading once the account exists).
4. You may need to renew the Group Pass annually.

A few notes on the license:
• Cooking, Games, The Athletic, and Wirecutter are *separate* NYT products *not* included — those require individual purchase.
• There's a *5 PDF download limit per day*.
• This resource is listed in the Library's A–Z Databases.

More info: <https://news.library.virginia.edu/2021/10/06/library-offers-free-access-to-new-york-times-digital-resource/|Library offers free access to New York Times digital resource>

The Virgo catalog also lists the *New York Times (website)* as an "Available online" journal record if you want to find it directly in the catalog: <https://search.lib.virginia.edu/sources/uva_library/items/u11886640|New York Times (website) — Virgo record>. (Note: the physical/microform *New York Times* newspaper is also held in Ivy storage, but the online Group Pass above is the easiest way to read it.)
